The lands between the railroad and 6th Street are zoned for light industry and would traverse an auto salvage yard and city owned lands. East of 6th Street the proposed facility will not be bridged over Grange Avenue since it will be vacated to the east for the proposed air cargo facilities.
East of the C.M. St. P. & P. Railroad the corridor swings to the northeast to the airport entrance road. The diagonal alignment of this corridor will leave triangular pieces of land but since Grange Avenue will be relocated north of the freeway between 6th Street and Howell Avenue, the area will be opened for new development. The land parcels that abut 3rd Street and extend to Howell Avenue have had recent commercial developments and would be displaced by this freeway facility.
Since the concept of this corridor was to re-align Corridor #3 to be north of the new airport limits of the air cargo area, its new alignment meets Federal, State and local airport officials approval.
The alignment of the new corridor would be approximately 2,000 feet from Runway 7R and would not be parallel to it and therefore should not be misleading to landing aircraft. The aeronautical study of this proposal has disclosed that the preliminary lighting for the Airport Spur would not exceed federal regulations and would not be a hazard to air navigation.
